ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Act on Reporting and Use of Certain Financial Transaction Information (Act No. 8911, as amended by Act No. 19794 of March 24, 2023); Presidential Decree No. 33107, Enforcement Decree of the Act on Reporting and Use of Certain Financial Transaction Information; Financial Services Commission Regulation on Customer Due Diligence and Beneficial Owner Identification; Act on the Regulation and Punishment of Concealment of Criminal Proceeds (Act No. 15623, as amended); FATF Recommendation 24 implemented through KoFIU guidance.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation (Certificate of Company Registration)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registry of Companies at the competent district court via the Supreme Court of Korea, Internet Registration Office (i-REG)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: For Hague Apostille states: obtain registry-issued certified copy and affix Apostille through MOFA. For non-member states: certified copy, notarize the registrar signature, then MOFA legalization, then legalization by the destination embassy/consulate in Korea. Apostille and consular legalization are mutually exclusive alternatives; never apply both sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing (Certified Corporate Registry Extract)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registry of Companies at the competent district court, Supreme Court of Korea
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille states: court-certified extract with MOFA Apostille. Non-member states: court-certified extract, notarization, MOFA legalization, and consular legalization by the destination mission. Use either path only depending on destination membership; do not chain Apostille and consular legalization.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution and Power of Attorney for Incorporation Representative
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Yuhan Hoesa Board and Notary Public in the Republic of Korea
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarize the corporate resolution and PoA; then for Hague Apostille states obtain MOFA Apostille. For non-member states, after notarization obtain MOFA legalization and then consular legalization by the destination embassy/consulate. The two routes are alternative, never cumulative.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association (Memorandum and Articles of Incorporation)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Yuhan Hoesa incorporators and Notary Public in the Republic of Korea
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: After execution and notarization, apply MOFA Apostille for use in Apostille states. For non-member states use notarization, MOFA legalization, and destination consulate/embassy legalization. Apostille and consular legalization are mutually exclusive channels; no sequential combination is permitted.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter from a Korean Banking Institution
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Korean commercial bank (e.g., Shinhan Bank, Hana Bank, Kookmin Bank)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Bank officer's signature is certified by the bank; if the destination requires authentication, notarize the officer's signature, then either MOFA Apostille (for Hague Apostille states) or MOFA legalization plus destination consular legalization (for non-member states). These are alternative paths and do not apply cumulatively.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National Tax Service of the Republic of Korea
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: NTS-issued certificate; for Hague Apostille states add MOFA Apostille. For non-member states have NTS certificate, notarize if necessary, MOFA legalization, then destination embassy/consulate legalization. Use either Apostille or consular legalization depending on the destination state; never both.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening must cover all shareholders at or above 25%, directors, officers, and authorized signatories against the OFAC SDN and non-SDN sanctions lists, UN Security Council consolidated lists (including UNSCR 1718 and 1988), EU consolidated list, UK HMT OPSI, and the Republic of Korea domestic designation list administered by KoFIU and the Ministry of Foreign Affairs. PEPs defined under FATF Recommendation 12 must be identified via World-Check/Refinitiv or equivalent and escalated to the MLRO. Screening is performed pre-engagement, at least annually, and upon ownership changes. Adverse hits trigger enhanced due diligence, freeze decisions, and Suspicious Transaction Report (STR) filing under the Korean Specific Financial Information Act.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Korean Supreme Court, Internet Registration Office (i-REG) Company Name Search and Reservation System (https://www.iros.go.kr)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under the Korean Commercial Act and Commercial Registration Rules, the trade name of a Yuhan Hoesa must be stated in Hangeul. A foreign name may only be recorded as a phonetic transliteration, with the original Latin characters appearing as a secondary name. The mandatory four-tier naming structure is: (1) geographic or business marker; (2) distinctive trade name; (3) business activity description; and (4) legal-form suffix yuhanhoesa (LLC). Hanja and foreign scripts cannot replace Hangeul in the registered trade name. Where an English brand is used, the registry will record the government standard romanization of the Hangeul name.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If i-REG returns a name rejection, the applicant has 14 days to remediate and resubmit through the same portal. If the rejection is repeated, a written objection may be filed with the registration court, which must re-examine the grounds under the Commercial Act. If denied, an administrative lawsuit may be filed within 90 days of the final written disposition. The objection must include revised name alternatives, evidence of consents for sensitive tokens, and a legal memorandum distinguishing the rejected name from prohibited marks.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Pure virtual offices are generally not accepted

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea, as amended, Chapter on Limited Liability Company (Yuhan Hoesa), Articles 287-2 through 287-46, together with the Non-Contentious Litigation Procedure Act and the Act on Consumer Protection in Electronic Commerce for e-commerce activity.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registry Office (Registration Division) of the District Court having jurisdiction over the Company's head office; filings are submitted electronically through the National Court Administration Internet Registration Office (www.iros.go.kr) or physically at the court registry counter.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Registration of Establishment of a Yuhan Hoesa (Limited Liability Company), submitted together with the duly notarized Articles of Incorporation and all statutory attachments.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-in capital is imposed on a Yuhan Hoesa under the Commercial Act. The organizers may determine the capital amount in the Articles of Incorporation; however, the full amount of subscribed capital must be actually settled and evidenced by a capital deposit confirmation certificate issued by a licensed bank in Korea before the court registration is filed. national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea, operating the Home Tax Service (HomeTax) electronic portal at hometax.go.kr; Korea Customs Service (KCS) via UNI-PASS administers export declaration control for indirect-tax substantiation.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a foreign-owned Yuhan Hoesa: (1) complete incorporation registration at the local court Commercial Registry and, where foreign equity investment criteria apply, file a foreign direct investment notification with a Korean licensed foreign exchange bank or Invest KOREA; (2) within 20 days of commencing business, file the Business Operator Registration application with the competent District Tax Office administered by the NTS, using HomeTax or an NTS-ready agent, accompanied by the corporate registration certificate, articles of incorporation, foreign investment notification, proof of place of business, and documents identifying the ultimate foreign shareholder; (3) the NTS will issue the statutory Business Registration Certificate, whose unique Business Operator Registration Number also functions as the corporate TIN and VAT ID; VAT registration is embedded in this business registration and does not require a separate VAT form; (4) for a foreign non-resident seller that is not establishing a domestic entity but is nevertheless required to collect Korean VAT, the standard route is Non-Resident Business Operator Registration filed with the NTS through HomeTax, including designation of a Korean domestic tax representative under the VAT Act, a power of attorney, foreign business registration evidence, and a domestic address and account arrangement; the NTS then issues a VAT ID for the non-resident business, subject to the same electronic invoice and reporting obligations.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. Korean tax law is not a check-the-box environment: a Yuhan Hoesa is mandatorily taxed as a domestic corporation under the Corporate Tax Act and cannot elect pass-through treatment or a different indirect-tax entity status. No hybrid mismatch election is available in the VAT and GST regime.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Tax (VAT), statutory regime: the Value-Added Tax Act of South Korea
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general turnover registration threshold: VAT registration is mandatory from business commencement for a domestic Yuhan Hoesa LLC. The law uses a KRW 80,000,000 annual taxable turnover ceiling for simplified taxpayer treatment of qualifying small individual businesses, but a corporate e-commerce retailer is outside that simplified category. A foreign non-resident supplier supplying goods or electronic and digital services to Korea is also subject to mandatory simplified VAT registration from its first taxable supply, meaning no economic turnover threshold applies.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Under the VAT Act and the NTS electronic invoice system, every VAT-registered supplier must issue a statutory tax invoice for each taxable supply. Taxpayers required to issue e-tax invoices must transmit the invoice data to the NTS HomeTax National e-Tax Invoice System using the certified HomeTax XML and API interface or an approved third-party e-invoicing agent. South Korea does not currently operate a real-time per-invoice fiscal-clearance model and does not impose anti-fraud digital stamps; instead, the HomeTax system receives e-tax invoice data promptly after issuance and automatically reconciles it against VAT returns, customs export declarations in UNI-PASS, card-payment data, and bank foreign-exchange reports. Failure to issue, delayed issuance, or false issuance of an e-tax invoice gives rise to penalty tax under the VAT Act, and a zero-rated export invoice will be rejected if it cannot be matched to a valid UNI-PASS export declaration.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating is available under the Value-Added Tax Act export provisions where (1) the goods are sold to a foreign purchaser, including an overseas individual on an e-commerce marketplace, and are physically removed from Korean customs territory; (2) the export is covered by a formal export declaration filed with the Korea Customs Service through UNI-PASS; (3) the seller retains proof that title and risk passed to the foreign buyer outside Korea, supported by the export invoice, parcel or airway bills, and logistics tracking; (4) the sales proceeds are denominated in foreign currency and received through a Korean licensed foreign exchange bank or otherwise evidenced by a Foreign Exchange Transaction Certificate; and (5) for qualifying offshore services, including digital content and gaming services supplied to non-resident customers, the place of supply and consumption is outside Korea. Consumer-electronics parcel exports qualify where the export declaration is in the exporting Korean entity's name and the documented shipment leaves Korea within the permitted export period.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Proof of Export Declaration issued by the Korea Customs Service through UNI-PASS)
Marine Bill of Lading, Air Waybill, or combined parcel or consignment dispatch certificate
Foreign Exchange Receipt Certificate (Foreign Exchange Transaction Certificate or inward remittance certificate issued by a Korean licensed foreign exchange bank)
Zero-rated export e-Tax Invoice transmitted through HomeTax with a reference to the underlying export declaration
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: NTS and Korea Customs audit export zero-rating by cross-matching UNI-PASS export clearances, HomeTax zero-rated e-tax invoices, VAT refund claims, and bank-reported foreign exchange receipts. If the exporter cannot produce valid export clearance or the export proceeds are not repatriated within the six-month statutory foreign-exchange settlement period, unless a permitted extension is obtained, the supply is reclassified as domestic taxable supply. NTS will then assess the 10% VAT, charge statutory late-payment interest under the Framework Act on National Taxes, impose VAT penalty tax for false or unissued tax invoices and failure to report, and retroactively disallow input VAT credits previously claimed in connection with the purported export. Submission of forged export or foreign-exchange documents may additionally trigger penalties and criminal sanctions under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, the Customs Act, and the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea (BOK) and the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MOEF) acting as the foreign exchange authority under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Korean won is fully convertible for current-account activities: trade in goods, services, freight, insurance, commissions and ordinary business expenses can be settled freely through domestic foreign exchange banks. The capital account, however, is managed: non-resident equity contributions must be reported under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act, and any conversion of foreign currency into KRW must take place at a licensed domestic bank. Korea does not impose a mandatory surrender ratio on non-resident trade proceeds; export receivables can remain in foreign currency, but they must be collected within the six-month statutory settlement period and be traceable in the Foreign Exchange Information System. Profit and dividend remittances from a Yuhan Hoesa are legal, yet the paying bank will require audited or reviewed financial statements, proof that the equity interest is registered on the Korean registry, withholding tax clearance, and a copy of the board/shareholder resolution approving the distribution. Practical hurdles are the reporting discipline around foreign direct investment, the need to maintain complete trade documents in Korean or English, and the sensitive treatment of payments that exceed a plausible retail-electronics turnover; the external auditor's report and source-of-funds evidence will determine whether a dividend is remitted without further regulatory escalation.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, export proceeds must be collected within six months from the date of export declaration or the date the goods are loaded, whichever is applicable; banks may extend the deadline by up to six months for justifiable commercial reasons if the extension is requested and recorded before expiry. There is no fixed mandatory conversion percentage to KRW; the exporter may retain the receipts in a foreign-currency trade account at a domestic foreign exchange bank. However, the underlying obligation is a collection-and-repatriation duty: proceeds must enter a licensed Korean bank account, be reported in the Foreign Exchange Information System, and be matched to the export customs declaration. Receipts routed through unlicensed overseas digital accounts or held abroad beyond the statutory period are treated as a foreign exchange regulatory violation and may attract penalties.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Basic Operational KRW Account / Foreign Investment Capital Escrow Account
Enterprise Current Account with Multi-Currency Sub-Ledger / Export Proceeds Deposit Account
Capital Escrow Account for Foreign Investment / Import Settlement Account
FX Hedging and Corporate Ecommerce Settlement Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low for primary treasury clearing. Offshore digital EMIs such as Wise, Revolut and Payoneer are not licensed foreign exchange banks in Korea and are legally barred from opening domestic won settlement accounts or providing Korean IBAN-equivalent clearing rails. They cannot service the Yuhan Hoesa as a primary bank or liquidity provider. Their permissible use is limited to supplementary consumer collection channels, for example card or wallet receipts outside Korea, and all such proceeds must ultimately be swept by SWIFT into a licensed Korean bank account using compliant purpose codes. Using an unlicensed EMI for corporate disbursements creates AML exposure, foreign exchange reporting failures, and a refusal risk from the Korean financial intelligence unit.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: The statutory director(s) of the Yuhan Hoesa must physically appear in a South Korean branch for the first-time corporate onboarding; remote consular proxy opening is not generally permitted because Korean banks are required to identify the beneficial owner and the actual signatories in person or through an equivalent FATF-compliant procedure, which for foreign directors is not satisfied by consul authentication alone. After the account is opened, subsequent signatory changes can be made under a notarized and apostilled power of attorney; a video interview can support but never replace the initial physical identity verification.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident beneficial owners using a locally formed Yuhan Hoesa without a physical commercial footprint, triggering shell-company red flags.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified Korean commercial registry excerpts showing the full shareholding chain, apostilled or consular-legalized certificate of incumbency for each non-resident shareholder, notarized passport copies, proof of residential address and bank reference from the foreign shareholder, a group ownership/control chart to ultimate beneficial owner, source-of-wealth narrative, and an operational substance folder including the e-commerce website, warehouse/service-provider agreements, inventory records, and employment contracts.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Receipts flowing almost exclusively from online payment aggregators such as Stripe and PayPal, creating third-party settlement and card-not-present laundering risk.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Merchant agreements and KYC confirmation from Stripe/PayPal, settlement statements showing gross and net amounts, fee and payer country details, reconciliation against e-commerce orders, shipment tracking numbers, API-level booking data, refund policy, customer dispute logs, and demonstrable proof that settlement funds are deposited into the Yuhan Hoesa's licensed Korean bank account in its own legal name.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-value consumer electronics trade susceptible to invoice manipulation and dual-use goods scrutiny, exposing the bank to trade-based money laundering and sanctions risk.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed purchase orders, supplier price lists, commercial invoices with HS codes, air or sea bills of lading, Korean customs entry filings and tax invoices, serial-number inventory in-and-out records, warranty registration data, product-source certifications such as KC/CE/FCC, and an audited trial balance showing gross margins consistent with online electronics retail.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound shareholder capital remittance with a purpose-code mismatch or a history of rapid re-booking to finance unrelated outbound disbursements.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Foreign investment notification acknowledgment from MOEF/KOTRA with its unique registration number, SWIFT MT103 or MT202 trail from the foreign investor, confirmation letter from the remitting foreign bank, source-of-wealth report such as income tax returns, savings history or corporate liquidation evidence, share-issuance minutes, capital verification certificate from an external auditor, and a three-month forward cash-flow plan tying the injected capital to e-commerce inventory and working capital expenses.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: For a Yuhan Hoesa receiving non-resident equity, the foreign investor must file a foreign investment report with MOEF/KOTRA or through a licensed domestic bank before remittance. The Korean entity opens an Investment Capital Escrow Account with a Tier-1 commercial bank; the investor remits foreign currency by SWIFT MT103/202 using the foreign direct investment purpose code, the domestic bank converts the funds into KRW and credits the escrow account, and after share issuance the company files a post-closing foreign investment report to obtain the Foreign Investment Enterprise Certificate. The bank records the inward remittance in the Foreign Exchange Information System, verifies the capital purpose, and produces a capital verification confirmation; the funds must not be released to unrelated parties before statutory capital verification is completed.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For imports of consumer electronics for resale, the Yuhan Hoesa can pay via SWIFT MT103 through its designated foreign exchange bank after presenting the proforma/commercial invoice and customs declaration; for larger settlements, an irrevocable commercial letter of credit in sight or usance form may be issued under the bank's import facility. For exports, foreign buyers remit via SWIFT MT103/202 to the company's export proceeds account, and if a letter of credit is used, the Korean advising bank negotiates the documents and settles the proceeds. Documentary collections on a documents-against-payment or documents-against-acceptance basis are acceptable for established counterparties, but the company must maintain consistent transport and customs documentation to satisfy the Korean bank's trade-reporting obligations. All settlements must be classified under the correct Foreign Exchange Transactions Act purpose codes and reported through the bank's BOK reporting module.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Plain-vanilla foreign exchange forward contracts and FX swaps permissible for underlying trade receivables and payables, with notional capped at the actual exposure and maturity aligned to the settlement date.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) permitted for KRW-USD exposure where physical KRW settlement is impractical, but only through an authorized domestic foreign exchange bank with documentary proof of real commercial exposure; synthetic layering or speculative rolling is prohibited.

Cross-currency swaps and interest-rate swaps allowed only for long-term capital or financing obligations, limited to the notional of the underlying Korean entity debt or equity, and any restructuring must be reported to the relationship bank and the Bank of Korea where applicable.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Value-Added Tax final return for October 1 - December 31 and annual settlement for general taxpayers
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By January 25 of the following calendar year; next business day if the due date falls on a non-business day
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing additional tax under the VAT Act of 20% of the VAT payable or refundable amount if omitted, false-return additional tax up to 40% for fraudulent claims, daily late-payment interest at 0.022% from the statutory due date, and suspension or forced closure of business for prolonged non-filing.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Monthly employment income withholding return and payment (wages, bonuses, and similar remuneration)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By the 10th day of the month immediately following the calendar month in which remuneration was paid
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to withhold triggers an additional tax of 2% of the unwithheld amount; failure to remit withheld tax triggers late-payment interest of 0.022% per day, administrative collection proceedings, and potential criminal prosecution for unlawful diversion of withheld taxes.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual statutory-register audit, signature/date confirmation, and archival of the Register of Members, Register of Directors, Register of Charges/Mortgages, and Minute Book
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporate Secretary and representative director of the Yuhan Hoesa; records maintained at the registered office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually before the members' meeting approving the financial statements, normally by March 31 for a calendar-year company
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: No fixed monetary filing penalty, but defective or missing statutory registers may subject the directors to liability for breach of the duty of care, evidentiary disadvantages in litigation, administrative fines under court supervision, and restrictions in bank or M&A due diligence.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual members' meeting approval of the annual financial statements and income allocation/stoppage decisions
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Members of the Yuhan Hoesa; minutes recorded in the corporate Minute Book at the registered office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three months after the end of each fiscal year, i.e. by March 31 for a calendar-year LLC; no statutory filing fee
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to convene or approve financial statements within the statutory window can invalidate the profit distribution, create director accountability risks, impair the reliability of the corporate tax return, and expose the company to creditor challenge of irregular distributions.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate income tax return with attached balance sheet, income statement, and corporate tax calculation schedules
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By March 31 of the year immediately following the fiscal year; NTS-approved filing extensions must be observed if granted
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing additional tax of 20% of the underdeclared/unpaid corporate tax (minimum fixed surcharge where tax payable is zero), under-reporting additional tax of 10%, fraudulent or grossly negligent misstatement additional tax of 40%, daily delinquency interest at 0.022%, and eventual asset seizure, business closure, public designation as serious tax delinquent, and tax evasion prosecution.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Local income tax return (corporate portion) and payment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By March 31 of the year immediately following the fiscal year; extensions align with the corporate income tax filing extension
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Local tax surcharges for non-filing and under-reporting as prescribed by the Local Tax Act, generally 10% for under-declaration and 20% for non-filing plus daily late-payment interest, compulsory collection and seizure, and administrative restriction of the business license for habitual delinquency.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Foreign-Invested Company Annual Report (only if a foreign investor holds 10% or more of the equity or capital contribution)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy through Korea Trade-Investment Promotion Agency (KOTRA)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 90 days after the end of the fiscal year, meaning by March 31 for a calendar-year company
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fine of up to KRW 5,000,000 for failure to file without justifiable cause, loss of foreign-invested enterprise recognition, downgrading of investment protection guarantees, and potential forfeiture of tax incentives or FDI support programs.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: External audit report submission to the financial regulator (only if statutory audit thresholds are triggered)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Supervisory Service (FSS) through the Data Analysis, Retrieval and Transfer System (DART)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 15 days after the annual members' meeting approves the audited financial statements; for a calendar-year company holding the meeting by March 31, this normally means by April 15
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to submit the required audit report subjects the company and responsible representatives to administrative sanctions under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies, fines, designation for inspection by the FSS, adverse tax audit treatment, and disqualification of certain director benefits.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Value-Added Tax preliminary return for January 1 - March 31
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By April 25 of the current calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing and late-filing surcharges under the VAT Act, commonly calculated as 20% of the tax payable, plus daily late-payment interest and suspension of tax invoices or business operations for repeated non-filing.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Value-Added Tax final return for April 1 - June 30
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By July 25 of the current calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing additional tax of 20% of the VAT payable or falsely refunded amount, false-return penalties, daily late-payment interest, business closure, and mandatory inspection for habitual violation.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Value-Added Tax preliminary return for July 1 - September 30
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By October 25 of the current calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing additional tax of 20% of the VAT payable, under-reporting additional tax, daily late-payment interest, and forced business closure or bank account seizure for continued delinquency.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Event-driven Commercial Registry filing for changes in members, directors, capital contribution, or registered office (not annual if no change occurs)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Supreme Court Commercial Registration Registry through the competent district registry office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days from the relevant corporate event; no annual filing required in years without a registrable event
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to register within 30 days may result in court-administered order for compulsory registration, additional court fines for non-compliance, inability to assert the change against third parties, and personal liability of the representative director for losses caused by delayed registration.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies, an independent external audit by a certified Korean CPA or licensed audit firm is mandatory where (a) total assets at the end of the immediately preceding fiscal year equal or exceed KRW 12,000,000,000; (b) the company is designated by the Financial Services Commission where total assets equal or exceed KRW 6,000,000,000 and there is a high investor-protection risk profile, such as total liabilities, deficient filing history, or substantial recurrent revenue; or (c) the company is a foreign-invested enterprise required by applicable foreign-investment regulations or government approval conditions to submit audited financial statements. Korean external audit law does not impose a separate employee-headcount audit trigger; headcount is not a statutory threshold in Korea, but revenue and asset-based large-corporation taxation remains subject to separate informational disclosure requirements.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Listed companies and companies required to issue public disclosures apply full Korean International Financial Reporting Standards (K-IFRS). A private Yuhan Hoesa not listed on a securities exchange and not otherwise designated may prepare its statutory financial statements under Korean Accounting Standards for General Business Entities (Korean GAAP / K-GAAP), while retaining the option to apply full K-IFRS. All statutory audits must be performed in accordance with Korean Standards on Auditing, which are aligned with International Standards on Auditing, and filed through the external audit reporting system.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Korea grants progressive corporate tax reductions for SMEs, R&D tax credits, foreign-investment tax credits, enterprise city and free economic zone incentives, and a 5-year tax holiday for new SMEs in certain sectors; online retail of consumer gadgets is eligible for standard deductions but will be taxed at 9% to 24% marginal brackets depending on taxable income.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Corporate Income Tax Return for Taxable Base and Tax Computation (Form 3 of the Basic Corporate Tax Schedule) filed via the National Tax Service HomeTax electronic portal
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 3 months after the end of the fiscal year; for Yuhan Hoesa with a December 31 year-end, no later than March 31 of the following year, with a possible 1-month extension when a certified tax agent prepares the filing.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, corporate registration number, head office address and representative director particulars.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: File under the exact BRN issued by the Korean district tax office; if the ultimate beneficial owner is a non-resident, the director must still list a Korean address for service and attach a power of attorney if a Korean tax agent files the return.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Business type classification and principal industrial activity (ISIC 4791, online electronics retail).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Describe the actual e-commerce operations, including the platform model, inventory warehousing and settlement providers (Stripe/PayPal); the description must be consistent with customs declarations and platform sales reports to avoid triggering non-resident PE or permanent establishment audit triggers.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income computation with the reconciliation of accounting profit to tax base.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include worldwide taxable income for this Korean resident LLC; deduct all arm's length operating expenses; separately identify cross-border related-party transactions because they must be reported and supported by transfer pricing documentation in compliance with Law for Coordination of International Tax Affairs Article 5.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax deductions, exemptions and tax credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders cannot claim treaty benefits inside the Korean company's corporate tax return; the company must claim only domestic credits such as foreign tax credits and R&D incentives; attach evidence if foreign taxes were paid on foreign source income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Detailed statement of cross-border transactions with non-resident related parties and of withholding tax obligations.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disclose each dividend, interest and royalty payment to a non-resident; state the applicable domestic WHT rate and treaty rate; attach the tax office approval of the treaty-reduced rate, payee tax residency certificate and beneficial ownership declaration before reporting the payment.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to file or late filing triggers additional tax under the Framework Act on National Taxes: 20% of the unpaid tax for under-reporting and 40% for fraudulent no-filing, plus daily overdue interest; deliberate misreporting of cross-border retail revenue will be referred for criminal prosecution with fines up to triple the evaded tax.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 22% statutory outbound dividend withholding tax (20% corporate income tax plus 2% local income tax surcharge), subject to reduction under an applicable Korea double tax treaty.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Before payment, Yuhan Hoesa must submit an Application for Approval of Tax Treaty Exemption or Reduction with the Korean tax office, attaching the beneficial owner's Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) issued by the resident tax authority, a beneficial ownership declaration stating that the owner receives the dividend for its own account, and, where applicable, an audited certificate that the shareholder has held at least a 25% interest for at least 12 months. The remitting Korean company must not apply the reduced rate until the tax office approves or accepts the application; if treaty relief is denied, the full 22% must be withheld and remitted.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory domestic WHT for outbound royalty and interest payments is also 22% (20% plus 2% local surcharge); applicable Korea DTA provisions commonly reduce interest to 10%-15% and royalties to 10%-15%, with strict beneficial-ownership and limitation-on-benefits conditions. Interest paid on bona fide financial debts to unrelated foreign lenders may be exempt under specific rules, but related-party debt must satisfy thin capitalization and arm's length pricing.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: KRW 10 billion in aggregate cross-border related-party transactions for the annual Local File; KRW 50 billion threshold for the Master File and KRW 1 trillion consolidated group revenue for the CbC Report; disclosure of related-party transactions with the NTS is also required if the aggregate exceeds KRW 100 million.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Korean tax authorities apply substance over form and may disregard shell corporate vehicles under the Framework Act and international tax abuse doctrines; for e-commerce, the Core Income-Generating Activities that create business profits must be performed and managed in Korea if Yuhan Hoesa is a Korean resident; a company with no Korean business substance, real employees, local management decisions or core retail activities will fail economic substance scrutiny, and related-party payment arrangements aimed at stripping Korean profits will be recharacterized.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion and False Corporate Filing
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately omitting online consumer electronics sales or routing payment transactions through PayPal/Stripe accounts held outside Korea to reduce the Corporate Income Tax return tax base; fabricating expense invoices or under-declaring sales as intercompany consignment transfers.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Article 3 of the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act, evasion of corporate tax is punishable by imprisonment up to 3 years or a criminal fine of up to 3 times the evaded tax; the NTS will also assess additional tax of 40% of the fraudulent under-reporting plus daily late-payment interest and impose a public disclosure as a high-value tax delinquent.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The court may pierce the corporate veil where the LLC is merely a façade, holding directors personally liable for civil restitution of evaded tax and penalties; responsible directors may be subject to asset seizure, travel ban/blacklisting, and criminal imprisonment up to 3 years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company and Economic Substance Failure
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating KR_YUHANGHOESA with no physical office, no Korean employees and no Korean management, while paying intercompany fees or royalties to related foreign traders to shift profit abroad; falsely claiming treaty benefits through a conduit shareholder with no active business.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Framework Act on National Taxes and the Law for Coordination of International Tax Affairs Article 6, the tax authority may disregard the legal form, reattribute profits and impose a 20%-40% penalty on the adjusted tax base plus criminal referral for abuse of tax treaty.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly maintain a sham structure lose limited liability protection under the Korean Commercial Act, becoming jointly and severally liable for the taxes and penalties; Korean courts may issue exit bans and order arrest or imprisonment for directors who transferred assets abroad to frustrate collection.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Cross-Border Withholding Tax and Repatriation Evasion
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying dividends, royalties or interest to non-residents without withholding the domestic 22% WHT, or applying a treaty-reduced rate before obtaining tax office approval; concealing profit repatriation through management fees or fake marketing service charges.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Corporate Tax Act and the Framework Act on National Taxes, the withholding agent is liable for the uncollected withholding tax, an additional tax equal to the unpaid withholding amount plus a 10%-50% penalty for willful failure, and daily overdue interest; criminal prosecution for tax evasion also applies.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who direct the non-withholding or authorize false invoices are jointly liable for the withheld corporate tax amounts; personal bank accounts of directors may be attached, and directors may be blacklisted with travel restrictions and face criminal imprisonment for fraud in connection with the repatriation of profits.
